title: POEM 04 · "I PUT THEM BACK ON"
about: WYGWYL poem 04: the clouds meet the stars, she searches the bare ground for her two hands, a 1969 man at a ship's rail laughs, and she puts her hands back on.
line: I put them back on with the care of my future at stake.

states.visible: she stands in the night garden; her arms end at the wrist tabs; her two hands lie on the ground ahead, in shadow
the 1969 sky wipes down into the plate's own sky, behind the spires; labelled; the garden darkens
she kneels: toes pinned, shins turn about them, both knees land; dust
she bows and pats the bare ground twice with her wrist stub; nothing there; dust rises and stays on the stub
a warm light finds the two hands; she sees them
a 1969 man at a ship's rail rises on a stick behind the ledge (labelled); from "find" his film runs: he turns and laughs
she lifts both wrist stubs and looks at them; the 1969 sky goes back up; the man stays
she bows and presses the near wrist onto hand A; the brad goes in
hand A, now hers, reaches for hand B and pinches its top edge
she rises carrying B; a held stop on "care"; the far wrist comes to meet it
B goes onto the far wrist on "stake"; A lets go
she holds both hands up and looks at them; on "nevermore" they go down to rest on her thighs; both stay dusty

contacts.what: near toe pinned in world space for the whole passage; far toe planted except for one logged step during the kneel
both knees on the ground (toes stay pinned)
near wrist stub on bare ground (wrong attempt 1)
near wrist stub on bare ground (wrong attempt 2)
near wrist stub onto hand A's wrist tab (hand A lying on the ground)
brad in: hand A now parented to the near forearm; lifted off the ground
hand A pinches hand B's top edge (B leaves the ground, parented to A)
brad in: hand B onto the far wrist (B parented to the far forearm)
hand A lets go of hand B; marked released, not zero

material.dust: particles spawned at each ground contact fly, land and stay as specks; stub dust 0 -> 0.35 -> 0.6 at the pats; both hands carry ground dust (0.55) from the start to the end
material.darkness: plate darkens to 0.42 by "darkness", eases to 0.18 when the 1969 sky withdraws
material.light: a warm light on the ground from "two hands" on, brighter after the sky clears
material.sky_wipe: torn wipe edge descends to y 900 over 364.4-367.5 s, rises on "mine"; drawn only inside the plate's sky mask
material.citizen_film: his frames 256-304 play at 29.97 fps from "find"; before that frame 256 is held, after it frame 304 is held

cameras.rule: wide for the sky, in on the wrong attempts, out for the citizen, close on the hands, back out for nevermore

joins: the 1969 sky wipes into the plate's own sky (its sky mask), behind the spires, labelled while it shows
the 1969 man rises as a cut-out on a stick behind the plate's ledge; his film plays inside one fixed scissor cut; tagged
her wrist stubs find her own loose hands; one hand carries the other to the far wrist; every hand-off is a logged contact
ledger: Her voice, 364.0-392.6 s of the WYGWYL suite recording. Word times by faster-whisper (small).
Eagle Has Landed: The Flight of Apollo 11 (1969), clip 6bb6d333 (source film 1513.81-1523.96 s), silent in this library. The man at the rail: frames 256-304.
The 1969 sky: a per-pixel median of the clip's own sky pixels; where no frame shows sky it is filled by a smooth blur.
The night garden: WYGWYL poem 04 AI plate (keyframe 84, held). The ledge is cut from it.
The puppet (reused from p07) and her second, open hand (generated). The rule that her hands come off and go back on.
The ground strip, the stick, the dust, the light, the labels.
"They too used to be mine": hers, about her hands. The 1969 man is not her memory and is not presented as one.
